items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Of course, Celestine always read music, just like Manuel Perez, you see.

ctx.x: Then they'd pick up a, oh, man, I swear to God, that people played so long, man. Oh, man.

Now, the only time they would play short, they'd play orchestration, you see. Well, they'd play it down. And if it was a good orchestration, you know, that they liked, well, they'd go back to the chorus and play one or two, you see. Of course, Celestine always read music, just like Manuel Perez, you see. Always had musicians in their reach, you know. It felt like Buddy Pettine, you know.

You know, when I used to go out to Tyler's Beer Garden? Who? To Tyler's Beer Garden during the war. I don't think you were ever out there. No, I don't. But Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman had the band. Tillman played with us?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Because, you know, my bands I played with, they didn't do it. Manuel Perez, Ridgely, no, they didn't do that, no.

ctx.x: Yeah, just a drum break. Very few of them done it. Many of them, you know, many of them didn't do it. Because, you know, my bands I played with, they didn't do it. Manuel Perez, Ridgely, no, they didn't do that, no.
I hear some of the white guys call that a turn around. Yeah, I see they do that, yeah.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: After I left Manny Perez. You mean the orchestra when I was playing on the roof garden?

ctx.x: After you left Perez, who did you play with? After I left Manny Perez. You mean the orchestra when I was playing on the roof garden? Mm-hmm. I told you I went down to La Vida. You went to La Vida. And then? Got with Ridgely. You with... With Bebe Ridgely's Tuxedo. That band split up at the time. Yeah, see that band split up at the time.
The Celestan's part of them or something? That's right, that's right. And how long were you with Ridgely?
